description: Two-tier candidate-capture wiring (2026-08-24). PostToolUse/Bash runs post-bash-candidate-queue.sh — pure POSIX shell, no subprocess heavier than `date`/`cut`, appends a JSONL line to ~/.claude/procedural-memory/candidate-queue.jsonl when a Bash call matches a known test/build invocation. It never checks an exit code: PostToolUse for Bash was found empirically NOT to fire at all when the tool result is an error (see the script's own header), so any invocation reaching this hook already succeeded. Stop runs session-end-scan.py — the heavier scan: fast-exits unless the queue has pending entries for this session_id, then cross-checks the transcript and surfaces promotion candidates. Deferred from the original scaffold note (still not built): a PreToolUse guard on Bash for a raw `rhize-skill`/venv-path invocation, and a PostToolUse nudge after Write/Edit. Both remain out of scope for this change. SessionStart runs session-start-env.sh (2026-09-15): appends `export PROCEDURAL_MEMORY_PLUGIN_ROOT=<plugin root>` to $CLAUDE_ENV_FILE so Bash tool calls can reach scripts/rhize-skill-launcher.sh by an absolute path — Claude Code substitutes ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} into config text but never exports it to the shell (measured in claude plugin eval and in a normal session). Advisory-only, exit 0 always, no subprocess heavier than pwd.
